I feel on guard even inside my own home
I frequently look behind me to check if someone is following me

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop

The world is a dangerous place
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

issues.explanation: 'Risky Behavior' is poorly integrated with the rest of the profile. The other threat items reflect hypervigilance and perceived danger (silence, being on guard at home), while memory and appraisal items center on intrusive, overwhelming captivity memories and beliefs that the world is dangerous or that she is 'going crazy.' Risk-taking points toward a different behavioral pattern that is not supported elsewhere, especially with Maladaptive Strategies absent and Threat not strongly linked outward in the formulation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Life Not Worth Living
issues.explanation: 'Life Not Worth Living' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the selected appraisals, which otherwise focus on danger and loss of control ('world is dangerous,' 'going crazy'). It introduces a severe hopelessness/suicidal cognition not echoed in memory, threat, or strategy items. At PCL-5 53 severe symptoms are plausible, but this specific appraisal is insufficiently supported by the rest of the profile and feels clinically disconnected rather than integrated.

vignette: Sofia's eyes would often glaze over, her mind transported back to that fateful night eight years ago when she and her partner were held captive by a group of assailants while responding to an emergency call. The memory was etched in her brain like a scar – the sound of shattering glass, the feeling of being dragged away from the safety of their ambulance, the smell of sweat and fear that clung to her skin long after they were finally freed. Even now, as a seasoned paramedic with over three decades of experience, Sofia couldn't shake off the sense of helplessness that crept in whenever she thought about that night. "I was so powerless," she would whisper to herself, "I couldn't even protect myself." As she delved deeper into her memories, the emotions came flooding back – a tidal wave of feelings that left her breathless and disoriented. It was as if the experience had become a living, breathing entity that threatened to consume her at any moment. When the memories resurfaced, Sofia felt like she was drowning in an ocean of fear, unable to keep her head above water. Her mind would start racing, her thoughts careening wildly from one catastrophic scenario to another – what if they came back? What if she wasn't prepared? The more she tried to push the memories away, the more they seemed to force their way into her consciousness, unbidden and unwelcome. Sofia had come to believe that her reactions since the event were a sign of her own fragility – proof that she was indeed going crazy. She felt like she was walking on eggshells, never knowing when the memories would strike again or what new horrors they might bring with them. Her world had shrunk to a tiny, suffocating space where every silence seemed menacing and every shadow hid a potential threat. Even in her own home – that supposed sanctuary – Sofia felt like she was constantly on guard, waiting for the other shoe to drop. As she navigated the familiar streets of her neighborhood, Sofia found herself frequently checking behind her, half-expecting to see someone lurking in the shadows. Her friends and family had grown accustomed to her nervous habits – the constant looking over her shoulder, the way she would freeze at sudden noises – but they couldn't understand why these behaviors persisted long after the trauma should have faded into memory. Sofia herself didn't know; all she knew was that the memories had become a constant companion, one that whispered dark fears in her ear and refused to let her go. Despite her best efforts to keep them at bay, the memories continued to haunt Sofia – an unwelcome presence that seeped into every corner of her life. It was as if they had developed a twisted symbiosis, feeding off each other's darkness until the threat felt omnipresent and suffocating. And yet, it was this very cycle that kept Sofia trapped in a prison of her own making – afraid to confront the memories head-on, too scared to let go of the fears that bound her. As she sat in her living room now, surrounded by the familiar comforts of home, Sofia felt like she was staring into an abyss. The memories loomed large, casting long shadows across her mind and heart. She knew she couldn't keep running from them – not anymore. With a deep breath, she reached for the phone and dialed the number of a therapist, hoping against hope that someone might finally be able to help her break free from this prison of fear and silence.
